extracted.intended_audience: K-12 teachers and instructional leaders implementing SRSD to meet Common Core/state writing standards
extracted.subtask_short: SRSD alignment to Common Core writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using the Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD) instructional framework to teach Common Core (and state) writing standards across argumentative, informative/explanatory, and narrative genres. Focuses on strategies, routines, and assessment alignment for classroom practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argumentative writing / Writing Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must be able to write well-structured arguments that support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence. This involves developing a clear thesis or claim, supporting the claim with logical reasoning and evidence, addressing counterarguments and refuting them effectively, and organizing writing coherently and persuasively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD teaches specific strategies for argumentative essays such as POW + TREE: Pick their ideas, Organize their notes, and then Write and say more. TREE guides students to create a clear Topic sentence, provide Reasons to support their claim, Explain the reasons, and end with a strong Ending. Aligns directly with CCSS requirements for well-supported arguments with logical reasoning and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informative / Explanatory writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Students need to write to convey information clearly and accurately by introducing and explaining a topic, using relevant facts, definitions, and details to develop the topic, and organizing information in a clear, logical order with appropriate headings and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD uses strategies like POW + TIDE for informative writing (Topic, Important details, Ending) to help students structure their essays, ensure logical inclusion of relevant facts and details, and use technical language and transitions to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative writing involves telling a story or recounting events coherently and engagingly. Students must develop characters, settings, and plot; use dialogue, description, and pacing; organize events in a logical sequence; and use narrative techniques such as flashbacks, foreshadowing, and multiple perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD strategies for narrative writing include POW + WWW, What=2, How=2 to help students plan and organize stories by focusing on who, when, where, and what happens. Emphasizes planning, organization, and story elements to meet Common Core narrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and coherent writing (organization & flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: Across genres the Common Core emphasizes clear, organized, and coherent writing: logical flow of ideas, effective transitions to connect ideas, and a clear introduction, body, and conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD teaches organization through graphic organizers and structured routines, and by explicitly teaching planning, writing, revising, and editing processes to ensure smooth flow and well-connected ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and synthesis (evidence integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must be able to conduct research to gather information, integrate it into their writing, synthesize information from multiple sources, evaluate credibility and relevance, and properly cite sources to support claims or explain ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD supports evidence-based writing by teaching students to use evidence to support claims and integrate information. Strategies like TREE encourage students to provide reasons and evidence and to synthesize information across sources for both short and extended research projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and editing
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards emphasize the importance of revising and editing: evaluating writing for clarity, coherence, and correctness; making improvements through revisions that strengthen arguments, narratives, or explanations; and editing for grammar, spelling, punctuation, and sentence structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD embeds self-regulation with revision checklists and self-assessment tools that prompt students to identify areas for improvement (e.g., add details, improve organization) and to perform edits that meet Common Core expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are expected to use technology for writing: publishing with digital tools, collaborating online to develop writing, and using online resources to gather and cite information for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD strategies can be integrated with digital tools (online collaborative platforms, research databases) to meet digital literacy aspects of the Common Core and to support publishing and research tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of grammar and conventions (language usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must use proper grammar, punctuation, and spelling, using standard English conventions and choosing words and sentence structures for clarity and style; they must understand and apply conventions appropriate to formal and informal writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD addresses language usage during the writing process, encouraging students to check for correct grammar and punctuation during revision. Aligns with Common Core Language Anchor Standards and emphasizes vocabulary acquisition and word choice for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-regulation and metacognitive routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must learn to self-regulate their writing process: plan, monitor, evaluate, and revise their work independently, using cognitive routines to manage challenges in organizing thoughts, developing ideas, and editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD's core emphasis is on self-regulation—explicitly teaching students strategies and self-monitoring routines (e.g., checklists, self-assessments) so they can break writing into manageable steps and track progress toward clarity, coherence, and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization tools: graphic organizers and structured routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should use graphic organizers and structured routines to plan and organize writing, ensuring ideas are well-connected and the piece has logical sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD incorporates mnemonics, graphic organizers, and step-by-step routines to teach planning, drafting, revising, and editing. These tools scaffold students toward independent, coherent writing aligned with Writing Anchor Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence to support claims (focused criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers must provide reasons and evidence to support claims, explaining how evidence connects to the claim and addressing counterarguments where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD's TREE explicitly prompts reasons and explanations; SRSD also teaches evaluating source credibility and integrating evidence across texts as part of research/synthesis practice for argumentative and informative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability to local/state standards and curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should be adaptable so that strategies and materials align with district, state, or international standards and specific curricula, even when those differ from the Common Core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD materials (graphic organizers, scripts, rubrics) can be adapted to fit local program sequences or upcoming conventions in a curriculum; teachers can begin with the genre their program follows and tailor rubrics and organizers to local needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary acquisition and effective word choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must build and use vocabulary appropriately, choosing words for effect and demonstrating command of varied word choice to communicate clearly and stylistically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD emphasizes vocabulary acquisition and language usage throughout instruction; teachers should integrate vocabulary teaching into writing tasks and revision to improve language competency per the Language Anchor Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding text types and purposes (genre awareness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must understand different text types (argument/opinion, informative/explanatory, narrative) and the purposes for writing each, and select appropriate features and structures for each genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD dovetails with genre instruction by teaching genre-specific strategies (e.g., TREE for arguments, TIDE for informative, WWW/What=2/How=2 for narratives) and by focusing lessons on text types and purposes required by CCSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment-aligned instructional design (preparing for NAEP/state tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should prepare students for standardized assessments (NAEP and state tests) that measure clarity, coherence, organization, evidence use, and genre-specific skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD's Writing to Learn course embeds Common Core language in rubrics and graphic organizers to align classroom instruction with assessment goals, helping students practice the logical thinking and clarity required by NAEP and state assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit teaching of planning, drafting, revising, and editing processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction must explicitly teach the stages of the writing process—planning, drafting, revising, editing—so students understand each stage's purpose and how to execute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRSD models and scripts the writing process, using mnemonics and routines to make each stage explicit; teachers provide guided practice with checklists and self-assessment to move students toward independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional use of mnemonics and scripted strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers should use mnemonic devices and scripted strategies to help students remember and apply multi-step strategies for different writing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include POW (Pick ideas, Organize notes, Write and say more) combined with TREE/TIDE/WWW/etc.; these mnemonics are taught, practiced, and gradually faded to promote independent strategy use.
